title: Search input has no associated label or aria-label — screen readers announce as unlabelled text field
detail: Line 145-149: the contracts search input has a placeholder ('Search customer, contract #...') but no <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby. Placeholder text disappears once the user types, and screen readers may not announce it. For external user testing with accessibility requirements, this is a gap.
evidence: ContractsList.jsx:145 React.createElement('input', { type: 'text', placeholder: 'Search customer, contract #...' ... }) — no aria-label property.
recommendedFix: Add 'aria-label': 'Search contracts' to the input's props object.

title: View switcher buttons lack aria-pressed or aria-current — active state not conveyed to assistive tech
detail: Lines 119-128: the view switcher renders three buttons (Smart List, Customer Groups, Split View). The active button is distinguished only by inline style (background/color swap). There is no aria-pressed or aria-current attribute, so screen readers have no way to convey which view is currently active.
evidence: ContractsList.jsx:121-126 — button has style change for active but no aria-pressed.
recommendedFix: Add 'aria-pressed': activeView === v.id to each view switcher button.

title: Loading skeleton is a plain gray box with no aria feedback — user unaware content is loading
detail: Lines 161-163: when data.loading is true and activeView is not 'C', the component renders a gray div as a placeholder. There is no text, no aria-busy, no aria-live region, and no spinner/animation. For external user testing, it appears as a static empty block with no indication of progress.
recommendedFix: Add aria-busy='true' and role='status' to the loading placeholder, or render a text-bearing spinner component consistent with other screens.

title: Modal overlay has no focus trap and no Escape-key dismiss — keyboard users are stranded
detail: Lines 296-336: the transition-confirmation modal is rendered as a fixed overlay. There is no focus trap (the user can Tab out of the modal into the background), no onKeyDown handler for Escape to close, and no role='dialog' or aria-modal='true'. A keyboard-only user or screen reader user who opens any status-change modal (Sent, Signed, Void, Decline, Close, Submit for Approval) may be unable to interact with it or dismiss it without a mouse.
evidence: ContractDetail.jsx:296 overlayStyle div — no role, no aria-modal, no onKeyDown for Escape, no focus management.
recommendedFix: Add role='dialog', aria-modal='true', aria-labelledby pointing to the modal title. Add onKeyDown handler that calls setModal(null) on Escape. Consider a ref-based focus trap on mount.

title: writeAuditLog failure in commitTransition is silently swallowed — audit gap invisible
detail: Line 102: `writeAuditLog({...}).catch(e => console.warn('Audit write failed:', e));` — if the audit log write fails after a successful status transition, the only signal is a console.warn. The user sees 'success' but the audit trail has a gap. For a compliance-sensitive contract workflow (Bancroft/SOX), a missing audit log entry could be material. The status change itself is already committed, so this is about observability not data integrity.
recommendedFix: Consider adding toast.show('warn', 'Status changed but audit log failed — please notify admin') so the gap is visible. Alternatively, feed the failure into the ErrorReporter buffer for Nora monitoring. Low priority since the status PATCH itself succeeded.

title: Loading state is a static gray box — no spinner or text indicator
detail:
Line 146: `if (loading) return
` — same pattern as ContractsList: a blank gray rectangle with no text, no animation, and no ARIA feedback. Users may think the page is broken rather than loading.
evidence: ContractDetail.jsx:146 — loading returns plain gray div.
recommendedFix: Replace with a centered spinner and 'Loading contract...' text, or add aria-busy='true' at minimum.

title: Generate Document button shows 'Generating...' text but is not visually styled as disabled state
detail: Line 168: the Generate button has disabled={generating} and toggles text to 'Generating...', but the button style (btnPrimary) does not change on disabled — it keeps the same navy background and pointer cursor. The HTML disabled attribute prevents clicks, but visually the button looks clickable. Users may click repeatedly thinking the first click didn't register.
evidence: ContractDetail.jsx:168 — disabled={generating} with static btnPrimary style. btnPrimary (line 355) has cursor:'pointer' and no :disabled styling (inline styles can't do pseudo-selectors).
recommendedFix: Add opacity: generating ? 0.6 : 1 and cursor: generating ? 'not-allowed' : 'pointer' to the button style when generating is true. Same pattern for modalSaving buttons at lines 330-332.

title: Hardcoded fallback company name 'Decades Contracting Group' in production render path
detail: Line 50: `c.dcfg_contractor_legal_name || 'Decades Contracting Group'` — when the contractor legal name is null, the component renders the literal string 'Decades Contracting Group'. Per feedback_no_customer_or_people_names_in_production.md, no customer or company names should appear as hardcoded strings in production code. The fallback should be a generic placeholder like an em-dash or 'Not specified'.
recommendedFix: Change the fallback from 'Decades Contracting Group' to a generic dash or 'Not specified'.

title: Document link uses emoji as sole link text — screen readers announce Unicode codepoint, not purpose
detail: Line 71: the document link renders emoji character (page-facing-up) as its visible text content. Screen readers may announce this as 'link, page facing up' or just a unicode codepoint, not 'View Document'. The adjacent text 'View Document' is part of the same text node but it's a different concern — the link text for accessibility should be the function, not the icon. Same pattern at ViewCustomerGroups.jsx:118 and ViewSplitPanel.jsx:53.
evidence: ContractRowDetail.jsx:71 — link text is emoji + 'View Document'. ViewCustomerGroups.jsx:118 — link text is only emoji. ViewSplitPanel.jsx:53 — link text is only emoji.
recommendedFix: Add aria-label='View document' to the anchor element. For ViewCustomerGroups and ViewSplitPanel where the emoji IS the sole content, aria-label is required.

title: Pagination renders ALL page number buttons at once — 20+ pages renders 20+ DOM buttons
detail: Lines 113-127: the pagination loop iterates from 1 to totalPages and renders a button for each. At PAGE_SIZE=50, a 1000-contract dataset (which hits the client-side cap) means 20 page buttons. This is a minor DOM bloat issue, not a perf crisis, but windowed pagination (show 5 buttons around current page) is the standard UX pattern and prevents the pagination bar from wrapping awkwardly on narrow screens.
evidence: ViewSmartList.jsx:114-127 — for loop from 1 to totalPages, renders one button per page.
recommendedFix: Render a windowed subset: current page +/- 2, with ellipsis buttons for gaps. Low priority — only matters at scale.

title: Expandable table rows use onClick but no keyboard interaction — cannot expand with Enter/Space
detail: Lines 86-100: each contract row has onClick to toggle expansion, but there is no tabIndex, onKeyDown, role='button', or aria-expanded attribute. Keyboard-only users cannot tab to a row or press Enter/Space to expand it. The expand/collapse chevron is visual-only (Unicode triangle).
evidence: ViewSmartList.jsx:86-100 — tr has onClick but no tabIndex or onKeyDown. Same issue: ViewCustomerGroups.jsx:73 customer headers have onClick but no keyboard handler.
recommendedFix: Add tabIndex={0}, role='button', aria-expanded={isOpen}, and onKeyDown handler that triggers toggle on Enter/Space to each expandable row. Same pattern for ViewCustomerGroups customer header divs.

title: useEffect syncing open-state creates new object every time grouped changes — triggers re-render cascade
detail: Lines 49-55: the useEffect watches [grouped] and calls setOpen(next) where next is a newly constructed object. Because grouped is recalculated by useMemo in useContractData on every page/filter change, this effect fires on every page turn, creating a new open-state object and triggering a full re-render of all customer group headers and their children. With 15+ customer groups visible, this is noticeable as a layout flash.
evidence: ViewCustomerGroups.jsx:49-55 — useEffect([grouped]) sets new open state object unconditionally.
recommendedFix: Use a functional update that only adds new keys without replacing existing ones: setOpen(prev => { var next = {...prev}; grouped.forEach(g => { if (next[g.id] === undefined) next[g.id] = true; }); return next; }). This avoids triggering re-render when the open state hasn't actually changed for existing groups.

title: Pagination uses arrow characters and different styling than ViewSmartList pagination
detail: Lines 128-139: ViewCustomerGroups renders its pagination with left/right arrow characters and opacity-based disabled styling, while ViewSmartList (lines 129-145) uses 'Prev'/'Next' text and color-based disabled styling. Both are in the same contracts section, and a user switching between View A and View B sees inconsistent pagination controls. The page numbering also differs: ViewCustomerGroups shows 'Page N of M' text; ViewSmartList shows numbered page buttons.
evidence: ViewCustomerGroups.jsx:132-138 — arrow chars, opacity. ViewSmartList.jsx:132-144 — text labels, color change.
recommendedFix: Extract a shared Pagination component used by both views. Low priority cosmetic issue.

title: doSearch catch swallows errors silently — search failure shows no feedback to user
detail: Line 83: `.catch(function() { setSearching(false); })` — if the fetchContractsPaginated call in doSearch fails (network error, 401, 403, 500), the catch clears the searching spinner but does not show any error to the user. The search panel reverts to 'Type a customer name...' as if nothing happened, and the user has no way to know the search failed.
evidence: ViewSplitPanel.jsx:83 — catch block only sets searching to false, no toast or error state.
recommendedFix: Add an error state: setResults([]); setResultCount(0); and render a 'Search failed — please try again' message. Or import useToast and show a toast on failure.

title: doSearch builds OData filter with user input but only escapes single quotes — no protection against OData injection
detail: Line 77: `var filter = "contains(dcfg_client_name,'" + val.replace(/'/g, "''") + "') ..."` — the val.replace handles single-quote escaping (correct for OData string literals), but does not escape other OData-significant characters. While the Web API endpoint behind Power Pages is unlikely to be vulnerable to injection beyond the OData query itself, the pattern is fragile. This is the same concern as CR-2026-04-09-0217 (portalApi escapeOdataString), but in a consumer file rather than the API layer.
evidence: ViewSplitPanel.jsx:77 — inline .replace(/'/g, "''") without using the centralized escape helper.
recommendedFix: Use the escapeOdataString helper added in portalApi.js per CR-2026-04-09-0217, or import it once it exists. This centralizes the escape logic.

title: Split panel search input has no label or aria-label — same accessibility gap as ContractsList search
detail: Line 119: the search input in the right panel has placeholder text but no aria-label, <label>, or aria-labelledby. This is the same gap as CR-2026-04-09-0700 but for the split-view's own dedicated search.
evidence: ViewSplitPanel.jsx:119 — input with placeholder but no aria-label.
recommendedFix: Add 'aria-label': 'Search all contracts' to the input props.

title: Split panel left side receives unfiltered contracts prop — attention filtering logic is absent
detail: Line 58-61: ViewSplitPanel receives props.contracts directly from the parent. The parent (ContractsList.jsx:176-178) passes data.contracts which is already filtered by viewMode. However, when activeView is 'C', the mode toggle is hidden (line 131), meaning the user cannot switch between attention/all. The left panel label says 'Needs Attention (N)' but if the data hook's viewMode is 'all' (set by a previous toggle before switching to view C), the left panel shows all contracts, contradicting its label. The split panel should apply its own attention filter independent of the shared viewMode.
evidence: ContractsList.jsx:176 passes data.contracts to ViewSplitPanel. ContractsList.jsx:131 hides mode toggle when activeView is 'C'. The left panel always shows whatever viewMode was set by the A/B views.
recommendedFix: ViewSplitPanel should filter its own attention contracts from props.contracts using the ATTENTION_STATUSES array from useContractData, or useContractData should expose attentionContracts as a separate computed property. This removes the dependency on the shared viewMode state.

title: Data tables (Exhibit A, Audit Trail) lack scope attributes on th elements
detail: Lines 249 and 276: the <th> elements in both the Exhibit A fee schedule and Audit Trail tables have no scope='col' attribute. This is a minor WCAG 2.1 compliance gap — scope helps screen readers associate data cells with their column headers in complex tables.
evidence: ContractDetail.jsx:249 <th> elements without scope. Line 276 same.
recommendedFix: Add scope='col' to all <th> elements in both tables.
